_note: Every visible string of a statement page's Lean file view and its 'What you must check' panel (scripts/lean_render.py). Placeholders in braces are filled from data. Plain words; no em dashes.

file.heading: The whole challenge file
file.intro: {lines} lines, exactly as in the release at commit {commit}. A name declared in this file links to its line, and hovering it shows its declaration.
file.legend_mathlib: Other linked names open Mathlib documentation (current) and show their underline when pointed at.
file.counts: Links in the file: {local} to its own declarations, {ext} to Mathlib’s documentation.

counts_imported.one: {n} more goes to the OpenAI modules the file imports.
counts_imported.many: {n} more go to the OpenAI modules the file imports.

counts_library.one: {n} declared name also links to the same declaration in OpenAI’s library.
counts_library.many: {n} declared names also link to the same declaration in OpenAI’s library.

counts_plain.one: {n} identifier stays plain because it resolves to no single declaration: a variable Lean binds automatically, notation, or a name the scan of the pinned sources did not find.
counts_plain.many: {n} identifiers stay plain because they resolve to no single declaration: variables Lean binds automatically, notation, or names the scan of the pinned sources did not find.

counts_ambiguous.one: {n} of them could name more than one declaration.
counts_ambiguous.many: {n} of them could name more than one declaration.

file.namespace_note: Names in the namespace {ns} are listed without it.
file.mathlib_note: OpenAI pins Mathlib at commit {mathlib}, and the documentation follows current Mathlib, so a name renamed since then may be missing there.

panel.heading: What you must check
panel.intro: A proof that Comparator accepts proves {theorem} as this file states it. These are the declarations its statement reaches by name, directly or through one another, each listed after everything it uses. A call written with dot notation, x.foo, counts every foo this file declares on its types, so the list may hold a declaration the statement does not need.

summary.one: It reaches {n} of the file’s {total} other declarations; with the theorem itself they span {lines} lines.
summary.many: It reaches {n} of the file’s {total} other declarations; with the theorem itself they span {lines} lines.

panel.intro_holes: This configuration names no theorem: Comparator checks that OpenAI’s library defines {names} with the type this file gives. These are the declarations reached by name from there, each listed after everything it uses.
panel.holes_note: A definition marked “name and type only” is checked by its name and type alone; a proof is checked against its body in OpenAI’s library, linked beside it, so compare that body with the one here.

summary_all.one: It reaches the file’s only other declaration; with the theorem itself they span {lines} lines.
summary_all.many: It reaches all {n} other declarations of the file; with the theorem itself they span {lines} lines.

panel.summary_none: The statement reaches no other declaration of this file.

summary_imported.one: It also names {n} declaration from the OpenAI modules the file imports, listed below.
summary_imported.many: It also names {n} declarations from the OpenAI modules the file imports, listed below.

panel.imported_heading: From the OpenAI modules the file imports
panel.imported_intro: The statement rests on these as well. They live in OpenAI’s library at the pinned commit, so read them there.

summary_direct.one: {n} of them is named in the statement itself.
summary_direct.many: {n} of them are named in the statement itself.

panel.rel_aria: Show what {name} uses and what uses it
panel.implicit_intro: Instances, notation and attributes take effect without being named, so the reference graph cannot follow them. Read these as well.

not_needed.one: {n} declaration the statement does not reach by name
not_needed.many: {n} declarations the statement does not reach by name

panel.not_needed_intro: The scan follows names in the text, so a declaration reached only through an instance or a macro is listed here.

script.card_library: The same declaration in OpenAI’s library at {commit}

page.formal_heading: Formal status: who has re-run it
page.readings_heading: What outside readers found about family {id}’s headline
page.readings_intro: These readings judge the family’s Lean statements against its headline as a whole, not this statement alone, each by the reader’s own published rules.
page.readings_link: The readings in full are on the family page.
page.draft_heading: OpenAI’s note, and an AI draft reading of it
page.alternatives_heading: Statements that share the most words with it
page.alternatives_more: Other statements that share words with it
page.alternatives_none: The backend records no other statement for it.

read_in_paper.candidate-pairing: Read the candidate theorem in the paper
read_in_paper.producer-cited-association: Read the cited theorem in the paper
read_in_paper.producer-declared-binding: Read the declared theorem in the paper

pair_line.candidate-pairing: Candidate pairing with {ref}, found by the words the two statements share. Nobody has reviewed whether they state the same thing.
pair_line.producer-cited-association: The Lean source cites {ref} by its label. Nobody has reviewed whether the two state the same thing.
pair_line.producer-declared-binding: The release’s manifest binds this declaration to {ref}. Nobody has reviewed whether the two state the same thing.

pair_heading.candidate-pairing: Candidate paper theorem: matched by shared words, not reviewed
pair_heading.producer-cited-association: Paper theorem cited in the Lean source, match not reviewed
pair_heading.producer-declared-binding: Paper theorem bound to it by the release, match not reviewed
pair_heading.unavailable: No paper theorem is paired with it

page.read_candidates: See the statements that share its words

pairing.shared: The two share {n} words, among them {words}.
pairing.alt_shared: Shares {n} words with it, among them {words}.
pairing.cited_how: The docstring of {declaration} names the theorem’s TeX label.
pairing.join_label: How the paper theorem and the Lean statement are linked
pairing.assoc_unresolved: The Lean source cites labels that do not resolve to a single theorem, so no theorem is paired.
pairing.no_record: The backend records no candidate theorem for this Lean statement.

runs.pin_other: at commit {pin}, not the release’s pin
runs.method: How they ran it, in their words
runs.reported: Each group below reports its own run; the atlas has not re-run it.
runs.none_recorded: No outside group reports a run of this Lean statement.
runs.scope: A re-run checks OpenAI’s proof against this Lean statement. It says nothing about whether the Lean statement matches the paper.

readings.defs: Definitions they ask a reader to check:

card.reruns_one: Re-run and accepted by one outside group at the release’s pin.
card.reruns_many: Re-run and accepted by {n} outside groups at the release’s pin.
